functions.subDef: Four podded turbofans produce thrust for all flight phases; in: fuel from collectors, throttle command from flight deck; out: thrust, engine parameter data to AVI (§5.1.1, §5.1.4). Independent per engine on separate pylons/zones (§5.1.5).
functions.funcDef: Produce and modulate propulsive thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).

functions.subDef: Two inboard-engine thrust reversers decelerate on the ground; deployment inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with mechanical lock (§5.1.2). Independent of forward-thrust production.
functions.funcDef: Produce and modulate propulsive thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).

functions.subDef: Two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers; ailerons on HYD B and C (§5.3.2). In: inceptor/autopilot command, air/inertial data; out: surface position to AVI. Independent surface/axis.
functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control the flight path across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: All-moving trimmable horizontal stabiliser with elevators; elevators on HYD A and C, with mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim (§5.3.2). Independent surface/axis.
functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control the flight path across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Split rudder in upper/lower segments each with own actuation and hydraulic supply (A upper, B lower); sizing case is outboard engine-out at V1 with max blade payload (§5.3.2-3). Independent surface/axis and segments.
functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control the flight path across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Double-slotted Fowler flaps in four sections and full-span leading-edge slats, two independent PDUs on common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes (§5.3.2). Distinct high-lift means.
functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to control the flight path across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: One twin-wheel nose unit and six three-wheel main bogies (20 tyres), tyre sizing for semi-prepared flotation; retraction on HYD A with free-fall alternate (§5.6.2). Distinct load-bearing/extension capability.
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, provide braking and directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.funcName: Decelerate and control on the ground

functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc, electrically signalled hydraulically actuated braking, normal HYD B / alternate HYD A / accumulator emergency, anti-skid per wheel pair (§5.6.2). Independent of steering.
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, provide braking and directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.funcName: Decelerate and control on the ground

functions.subDef: Hydraulic nose-wheel steering commanded from tillers and rudder pedals with mechanical disconnect for towing (§5.6.2). Independent of braking.
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, provide braking and directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.funcName: Decelerate and control on the ground

functions.subDef: Upward-hinging visor opened/closed on HYD A with electric backup drive; ground-only operation (§5.7.2, §5.7.6). In: HYD A, backup electric, crew/ground command. Distinct from lock function.
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in access to the hold and maintain pressure-boundary closure of the nose visor when closed (SDD §5.7.1). Door structural integrity excluded (treated as structure, §5.7.3).

functions.subDef: Twelve rotary latches on common torque shaft plus eight independent locking pins on separate supply; dual dissimilar lock sensing; pressure interlock below 0.1 psi before unlock (§5.7.2). Distinct from drive; provides lock status to take-off config monitor.
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in access to the hold and maintain pressure-boundary closure of the nose visor when closed (SDD §5.7.1). Door structural integrity excluded (treated as structure, §5.7.3).

functions.subDef: Nine saddles, two tension straps each by electric winches locked mechanically; lateral/vertical by saddle geometry; loss of one strap carried by neighbours (§5.8.2-3). In: EPS to winches, loading plan. Distinct from monitoring.
functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade of up to 72.6 t through all flight and ground load cases (SDD §5.8.1). Hold floor hard-point structure excluded (§5.8.3).

functions.subDef: Single instrumented tension loop annunciates strap tension loss in flight; two adjacent stations annunciated as restraint condition (§5.8.2). Distinct instrumented capability; single spanwise run recorded item.
functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade of up to 72.6 t through all flight and ground load cases (SDD §5.8.1). Hold floor hard-point structure excluded (§5.8.3).

functions.subDef: Two air cycle packs supplied via cross-bleed manifold, separate flight-deck and hold conditioning zones (§5.9.2). In: engine/APU bleed, ram air, EPS. Distinct from pressure control.
functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air and control fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).

functions.subDef: Two controllers drive two outflow valves (either sufficient), pneumatic backup, independent positive/negative relief; low hold differential (~8,800 m equiv, preliminary) (§5.9.2). Distinct pressure-control capability.
functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air and control fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).

functions.subDef: Wing leading edges and engine inlet cowls by hot bleed air; stabiliser leading edges electrically heated in six independent zones (§5.10.2). Distinct from probe heat.
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes in the icing envelope (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect airframe and inlets from ice

functions.subDef: Probes, static ports, windshields and two ice detectors electrically heated and individually monitored; detection advisory with automatic activation (§5.10.2). Distinct electrically-supplied means; detectors identical type recorded item.
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes in the icing envelope (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Heat probes and provide ice detection

functions.subDef: Four display units and two HUDs driven by three display processors on dual networks; three ADIRUs; standby instrument sharing no supply/sensor/processing (§5.11.2). Distinct from alerting.
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present flight, navigation and management information, and host prioritised crew alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subName: Acquire and present flight and navigation data

functions.subDef: Alerting consolidates every system's status into one prioritised crew alert list with procedures, driven by two independent processing channels (§5.11.2). Distinct dual-channel capability.
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present flight, navigation and management information, and host prioritised crew alerting (SDD §5.11.1).

functions.subDef: Dual-loop continuous detection per engine nacelle and APU (AND logic, degrading to single loop); bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat; nine-station hold smoke detection (§5.12.2). Distinct from suppression.
functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where required and provide extinguishing/suppression (SDD §5.12.1).

functions.subDef: Two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed to either nacelle; single dedicated APU bottle auto-discharged when unattended; hold has no suppression by decision (§5.12.2). Distinct discharge capability.
functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where required and provide extinguishing/suppression (SDD §5.12.1).

functions.subDef: Two HP gaseous cylinders on common manifold with crossover feed four quick-donning demand masks; no passenger oxygen (hold not occupied) (§5.13.2). In: crew donning, DC for indication only. Single behaviour; regulators independent per mask.
functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for depressurisation, smoke and fume events and the following diversion (SDD §5.13.1).

fha.effAc: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm beyond the rudder authority provided; aircraft yaws/rolls uncontrollably toward loss of control
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond crew
fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of propulsive thrust — asymmetric, exceeding available directional-control authority
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to arrest the yaw with available rudder authority; loss of directional control
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An asymmetry exceeding available directional-control authority leaves the crew unable to maintain controlled flight, tending to loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: No propulsive thrust available from any engine; aircraft cannot sustain flight and cannot reach a suitable aerodrome
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond crew
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of propulsive thrust
fha.effCrew: Crew faces forced descent/off-field landing with no thrust; not survivable at most phases
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of thrust from all four engines removes the ability to sustain flight, tending to loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Inboard reverser deploys in flight, producing large asymmetric drag/thrust and pitch/yaw upset; potential loss of control
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond crew
fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent reverse thrust deployment in flight
fha.effCrew: Sudden asymmetry and configuration change; crew workload extreme, control margin severely reduced
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: In-flight deployment of an inboard reverser produces an uncommanded asymmetry the crew may be unable to control, tending to loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Deployed inboard reverser will not restow; residual reverse drag/asymmetry during the landing roll on a semi-prepared strip
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond crew
fha.fcDesc: Reverser fails to stow after deployment
fha.effCrew: Crew manages an unstowed reverser during rollout; directional control effort increased
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect not derivable from the provided text: the SDD does not state the directional-control or landing-distance consequence of a single inboard reverser stuck deployed on the 1,800 m semi-prepared surface. Fill after determining rollout controllability/margin with one reverser unstowed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Reverse thrust unavailable when commanded at touchdown; deceleration relies on wheel braking alone against the 1,800 m requirement
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond crew
fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of reverse thrust availability at deployment
fha.effCrew: Crew expects reverse and does not receive it; may need to reassess stopping margin during rollout
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect not derivable: the SDD gives predicted rollout ~1,080 m against a 1,800 m requirement but does not state whether that margin holds without reverse thrust on a semi-prepared surface, so the overrun consequence cannot be classified. Fill after the braking/landing-distance assessment with reverse unavailable.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Reduced ground-deceleration contribution from reverse thrust; wheel braking and flotation remain available; stopping margin against the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement is reduced by an amount the SDD does not quantify.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of reverse thrust on ground
fha.effCrew: Crew apply braking normally; may perceive reduced deceleration and modulate braking/autobrake.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: SDD does not quantify the deceleration contribution of one reverser versus both, so the reduction in stopping margin against the 1,800 m requirement / ~1,080 m predicted rollout cannot be bounded. Engineer to supply landing-performance credit for reverse thrust.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: No reverse-thrust deceleration; deceleration relies wholly on wheel braking (dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve) and flotation on a semi-prepared surface; the operating margin between the 1,800 m landing requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout is eroded.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of reverse thrust on ground
fha.effCrew: Crew apply maximum available braking; increased attention to stopping distance and surface condition.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in ground-deceleration safety margin on a semi-prepared surface where the requirement/predicted-rollout margin is the design basis; braking remains available so a large reduction in safety margin is not supported. Proposed for engineer confirmation once reverse-thrust landing credit is established — if reverse thrust carries credited landing distance, severity may rise. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Roll surfaces move in a sense or magnitude other than commanded, producing an unintended bank/roll rate; fly-by-wire voting across three dissimilar computers is intended to detect and reject an erroneous command, so a passed-through erroneous response implies the protection has been defeated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to crew command
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the discrepancy between command and aircraft response and counter it; increased workload to maintain the intended flight path.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not bound the magnitude or transient of an erroneous roll response that survives the three-computer voting, nor the resulting attitude excursion or crew recovery margin. Engineer to define the credible worst-case erroneous roll authority and flight-phase exposure.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Roll surfaces deflect without a crew or autopilot command, producing an uncommanded bank/roll rate; each roll surface is driven by two actuators on different hydraulic systems (ailerons B and C), so an uncommanded deflection implies a runaway/hardover in an active path.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded roll motion with no command
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded roll and apply corrective input; increased workload and potential attitude excursion before recovery.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not bound the surface-deflection rate/authority of an uncommanded (hardover) roll input nor the recoverable attitude margin, so the effect cannot be graded. Engineer to supply the credible uncommanded roll authority and phase-dependent recovery assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: A roll surface is jammed at a fixed position; roll is a two-segment aileron plus multi-function spoiler function with dual actuation per surface from different hydraulic systems, so remaining roll effectors provide degraded but continued roll control depending on jam position and magnitude.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Roll surface jam
fha.effCrew: Crew fly with reduced/asymmetric roll authority and any trim/offset required to hold the intended flight path; increased workload.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not state the residual roll authority with one surface jammed at its worst-case position, nor whether the remaining effectors preserve full-envelope control, so the reduction in safety margin cannot be bounded. Engineer to supply post-jam roll authority and controllability assessment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: A steady erroneous roll bias is introduced without crew command and develops undetected; the aircraft holds an unintended bank / requires uncommanded roll input to hold wings level, producing a persistent lateral flight-path error and reduced lateral safety margin.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll bias developing undetected (malfunction, crew unaware)
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the source; may unknowingly trim or hold against the bias, increasing workload once the deviation becomes perceptible.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The provided function definition establishes that roll control is erroneous/biased but does not state the magnitude or rate of the bias, nor the flight-path deviation it produces before detection — the aircraft-level effect severity cannot be derived. Class not committed; supply bias-magnitude / detectability basis to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Roll control authority is reduced but remains within the manoeuvre/authority envelope; the aircraft is still controllable in roll for all required manoeuvres, with reduced margin against demanding lateral cases.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Degraded roll control authority within manoeuvre/authority envelope limits (partial loss)
fha.effCrew: Degradation annunciated; crew fly a degraded roll capability with slightly increased attention/workload and observe any restrictions.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effect chain: roll authority remains within the envelope and the aircraft stays controllable in all required manoeuvres, giving a slight reduction in safety margins / slight increase in crew workload. Committed at Minor per the stated effects; confirm the "within envelope" framing (see MAC assumption). [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Roll control authority is reduced below the envelope required for normal manoeuvring; the aircraft cannot achieve required roll response in demanding lateral cases, producing a large reduction in lateral controllability and safety margins.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold not occupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Degraded roll control authority outside manoeuvre/authority envelope limits (partial loss)
fha.effCrew: Crew face substantially increased workload and difficulty maintaining lateral flight path, potentially approaching the limit of achievable control in demanding cases.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effect chain: roll authority insufficient for required manoeuvres = large reduction in functional capability / safety margins plus excessive crew workload, consistent with Hazardous. Committed pending your confirmation of the "outside envelope" definition and the flight phases where it is most limiting (e.g. approach/landing, engine-out lateral case). [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Aircraft departs the intended flight path in pitch; an erroneous nose-up/nose-down response near the ground or at high speed can produce a large excursion in attitude, load factor and flight-path angle before the crew can counter it.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers or cargo attendants exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response to crew command — pitch axis responds in the wrong sense or magnitude to a flight-crew pitch input
fha.effCrew: Crew perceive an incorrect response to their command and must diagnose and counter it; high workload and potential for the corrective input to compound the error.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous pitch response is a loss of control of a primary trajectory axis; in the take-off/approach/landing phases a large uncommanded pitch excursion can exceed recoverable attitude/load-factor limits, supporting loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches without command, departing the intended flight path; magnitude and rate determine whether the excursion in attitude, load factor and flight-path angle remains recoverable, worst near the ground.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers or cargo attendants exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch motion with no crew command — pitch surface/trim moves the aircraft in pitch absent any flight-crew or autopilot input
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded motion, identify the source and arrest it; workload elevated and reaction time is critical at low altitude.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded pitch excursion on a primary trajectory axis, if of sufficient rate/magnitude in take-off, approach or landing, can exceed recoverable limits and result in loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: A jammed pitch surface or a runaway stabiliser to a large deflection produces a sustained pitching moment and a large out-of-trim condition; potential for a flight-path excursion beyond the authority of the remaining pitch means to counter, worst near the ground and at speed extremes.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers or cargo attendants exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Pitch surface jam or trim runaway — a pitch control surface jams or the stabiliser trim runs away to a commanded/uncommanded extreme
fha.effCrew: Crew face a large sustained out-of-trim force and reduced pitch authority; must counter with remaining pitch means or the mechanical reversion path to the stabiliser trim, at high workload.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A pitch jam or full trim runaway can leave insufficient pitch authority to maintain the flight path in a critical phase, supporting loss of the airplane; retained here as worst case for engineer confirmation against the pitch authority/reversion analysis. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: A slowly developing uncommanded pitch/flight-path deviation accumulates before the crew detect it, producing a gradual departure from the intended trajectory; end state depends on how far it develops before recognition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers or cargo attendants exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch developing below the crew detection threshold — a slow uncommanded pitch/flight-path change not annunciated and below the rate at which the crew perceive it
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware; recognition is delayed until the deviation becomes apparent, at which point the departure and any resulting out-of-trim may be large.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity turns on how far the flight-path/pitch deviation develops before it becomes detectable and on the crew alerting available for a slow pitch drift — the provided function definition and SDD do not state the detection threshold, the deviation growth rate, or the alerting coverage, so the resulting aircraft end-state cannot be grounded and no class is derived.. fha.effAc: A slow undetected trim runaway accumulates a large out-of-trim condition and a corresponding flight-path deviation; if undetected through a configuration/speed change (e.g. descent, approach) the mistrim and resulting excursion could be significant.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers or cargo attendants exposed.

fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware; the growing mistrim is masked until manifested as a control-force or attitude change, potentially at a critical phase.

SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the maximum out-of-trim reached before detection, the trim runaway rate, and the crew alerting for slow trim motion — none of these are stated in the provided function definition or SDD, so the aircraft end-state cannot be grounded and no class is derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Reduced pitch authority; aircraft controllable but with reduced margin to the flight-envelope limits and increased difficulty holding path in gusts/manoeuvre.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect beyond flight crew.

fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects are a significant reduction in safety margins/functional capability with significant crew workload increase, not rising to a large reduction while within MAC limits. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: A jammed rudder segment imposes a fixed yaw/roll bias and consumes directional control authority against the outboard-engine-out sizing case; the split upper/lower segment arrangement on separate hydraulic supplies is intended to leave sufficient authority on the remaining segment.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Yaw surface jam (rudder segment jammed at a deflection)
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to hold heading/trim out the bias; degraded directional handling.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects as stated (large reduction in directional safety margin / authority against the engine-out sizing case) support Hazardous; PROPOSED pending confirmation of remaining-segment authority with one segment jammed. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw developing below crew detection threshold
fha.effCrew: Crew assumed unaware and taking no corrective action; effect depends on the divergence rate and time to recovery, which the SDD does not characterise.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Effects assessment and severity require the flight-control divergence/recovery analysis before a class can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw bias developing undetected

fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity requires the flight-control bias-magnitude and detection analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Reduced directional control authority remaining within design limits; margin against the outboard-engine-out-at-V1 sizing case with maximum blade payload is eroded but not exceeded.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of yaw control authority within maneuvering/authority limits
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to maintain directional control, particularly in the engine-out / crosswind case.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Directional authority is shown by the SDD to be margin-critical (engine-out-at-V1 sizing case sets rudder area); a partial loss still within limits supports a significant reduction in safety margin — PROPOSED Major pending the engine-out directional-authority budget to confirm the margin remaining. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Directional control authority reduced below the design limit required by the outboard-engine-out-at-V1 sizing case with maximum blade payload; insufficient authority to trim/counter the sizing asymmetry.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of yaw control authority outside maneuvering/authority limits
fha.effCrew: Excessive workload; inability to maintain directional control in the engine-out sizing case.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of directional authority below the design-required level against the stated engine-out sizing case supports a large reduction in safety margins — PROPOSED Hazardous; confirm against the directional-authority budget whether any case is catastrophic (e.g. departure at V1). [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: No means to control yaw; directional control lost. With four engines on a 28 m outboard moment arm, an asymmetric-thrust or crosswind event cannot be countered — departure from controlled flight is credible; on the ground the take-off/landing case is unrecoverable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants in hold. Flight crew only exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of yaw control authority
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to arrest yaw/sideslip by any means; excessive workload with no effective response.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of yaw control removes directional control across all phases; with the outboard-engine-out sizing case a loss of control leading to loss of the airplane is credible. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Uncommanded flap/slat extension or retraction changes configuration without command; asymmetry or wrong-config at low speed reduces margins to stall or overspeeds the surface. Symmetric uncommanded change alters trim/performance; asymmetric change produces a rolling/yawing moment the crew must counter.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement without crew command
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter an unexpected configuration change and asymmetry, with increased workload at a critical phase.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Symmetric vs asymmetric uncommanded movement drive materially different effects (increased workload vs potential loss of control); the function definition alone does not fix which case governs, so the committed class is left for the engineer to set against the asymmetry-brake architecture.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Surfaces move to a position other than commanded (over/under-deployment or wrong schedule), changing lift/drag and stall/approach speeds versus the displayed configuration; performance planning is invalidated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous high-lift position response to crew command
fha.effCrew: Crew, aware via annunciation, reverts to the actual configuration and adjusts speed schedule — significant workload increase at a critical phase.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous-but-detected configuration invalidates the displayed performance schedule and imposes a significant workload increase; effects stated support a significant reduction in safety margins for the crew to manage. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: A high-lift asymmetry develops undetected, producing a rolling moment; with the crew taking no corrective action the asymmetry grows and, at low speed with the blade payload, can exceed lateral control authority and lead to loss of control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Slowly developing high-lift asymmetry below detection threshold
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware and continuing normal duties; no corrective action taken until the roll becomes apparent, by which time authority may be exhausted.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected, growing high-lift asymmetry with no crew action can exceed lateral control authority at low speed and lead to loss of control; the unaware case removes the mitigation that would otherwise cap severity. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: High-lift is available but at reduced capability; higher take-off/approach speeds and longer field length are required against the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement, eroding the margin above the ~1,080 m predicted rollout.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Degraded high-lift with reduced/partial deployment within limits
fha.effCrew: Crew applies the degraded-configuration procedure and revised speeds; increased workload but a defined, flyable case.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced high-lift capability within limits significantly reduces field-length/speed margins on a semi-prepared surface and increases crew workload, consistent with a significant reduction in safety margins. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Asymmetry brakes arrest the affected section, leaving a fixed high-lift asymmetry; roll/yaw trim demand and possible speed/configuration restriction until landing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment restrained by asymmetry brakes
fha.effCrew: Asymmetry annunciated; crew apply lateral trim and fly a restricted-configuration approach per procedure.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect on safety margin depends on the residual asymmetry the brakes leave and the roll/yaw authority remaining to trim it, which the SDD does not quantify; cannot derive a class between Major (significant margin reduction) and Hazardous (large reduction) without that data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: No flap/slat available; take-off and landing flown clean-configuration at markedly higher speeds; approach/landing speeds and distances increase, eroding the semi-prepared-strip landing margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of high-lift extension/retraction capability
fha.effCrew: Increased workload flying a non-standard high-speed configuration and managing landing-distance margin at a semi-prepared strip.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of all high-lift forces a clean-configuration landing at a semi-prepared strip whose margin (≈1,080 m rollout vs 1,800 m requirement) already rests on braking/flotation; a large reduction in safety margins with elevated crew workload supports Hazardous. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Crew believe gear locked when it is not; on touchdown the unlocked leg(s) may collapse, degrading ground support and directional control on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous downlock indication with gear not locked
fha.effCrew: No cue to take alternate action; false assurance until collapse at touchdown.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected not-locked leg carried to touchdown risks partial gear collapse and loss of ground support on a semi-prepared strip; a large reduction in safety margins with the misleading indication defeating crew action supports Hazardous. Note dual independent downlock sensing is claimed and must be assessed against this condition. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Reduced footprint flotation (e.g. loss of a bogie/wheels) increases ground pressure on the semi-prepared surface, risking rutting/sinkage, increased rollout and reduced directional control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground support / reduced flotation on semi-prepared surface
fha.effCrew: Increased workload managing directional control and rollout margin on the degraded surface.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Flotation was sized to a tactical-airlifter footprint and the gear/bogie count is explicitly preliminary and not frozen; without the flotation design case and the effect of losing one bogie on surface bearing and rollout, cannot derive whether margin reduction is significant (Major) or large (Hazardous).. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Normal (HYD A) extension failed and free-fall alternate not achieving downlock on one or more legs; landing on incomplete/unlocked gear degrades or loses ground support at touchdown.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Failure to extend to locked-down configuration
fha.effCrew: Crew execute alternate free-fall extension from separate handle; increased workload and possible need to land with incomplete gear.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Failure to achieve a locked-down configuration despite the free-fall alternate leads to landing on incomplete gear, a large reduction in safety margins at a semi-prepared strip; supports Hazardous. Catastrophic (total loss) not supported by stated effects given free-fall independence and unoccupied hold. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Downlock confirmation lost on one unit while the unit may in fact be locked or unlocked; with the crew unaware and taking no action, a gear that is not actually locked can collapse at touchdown on the semi-prepared strip, producing asymmetric loss of ground support and a runway excursion risk.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of downlock confirmation on one gear unit (crew unaware, continues normally with no action)
fha.effCrew: No annunciation of the affected unit; crew continue a normal landing with no corrective action available.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class from the provided material: the SDD states dual independent downlock sensing per unit but does not establish whether loss of one sensing channel leaves the actual mechanical lock state confirmed by other means, nor the touchdown outcome of an unconfirmed-but-locked vs unconfirmed-and-unlocked unit. The effect on the aircraft (collapse vs benign) is not determinable from the function definition alone — engineer to establish the true gear state and touchdown consequence before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot be supported by the gear at touchdown; gross structural contact with the surface, loss of controllability on the ground and probable loss of the airframe at maximum landing weight (318,000 kg) on a semi-prepared strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only, exposed to a survivability-limiting event.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground support capability at touchdown
fha.effCrew: No means to arrest or control the aircraft on the ground; survivability determined by the impact.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of ground support at touchdown at maximum landing weight results in loss of the airplane and likely fatalities to the flight crew — meets the Catastrophic anchor. Extremely Improbable safety objective applies (1x10^-9/fh, Part 25). [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Uncommanded or asymmetric braking induces a yawing moment and directional divergence during the ground roll; on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against a ~1,080 m predicted rollout, an asymmetric brake event risks a runway excursion or tyre/gear damage; anti-skid operates per wheel pair.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric or uncommanded wheel braking application
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to counter the yaw with steering and differential control; recognition and correction required during a high-workload ground phase.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class from the provided material: the magnitude of the yawing moment from a single asymmetric brake application, the countering authority available from nose-wheel steering and rudder on the ground, and whether the excursion is controllable within the ~720 m margin are not established by the function definition. Engineer to establish the controllability outcome and the number/energy of wheels affected before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Braking output does not correspond to the crew pedal command — either less than commanded, more than commanded, or in the wrong sense — degrading the crew's ability to schedule deceleration within the landing-distance margin and potentially inducing directional upset on the semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous braking response to pedal command (braking output differs from commanded)
fha.effCrew: Crew perceive incorrect braking authority; increased workload to re-establish control of the ground roll and detect the mismatch.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot commit a class from the provided material: the direction and magnitude of the error (under-braking eroding the ~720 m margin vs over-braking/wrong-sense inducing an excursion) is not fixed by the function definition, and the compensating means (autobrake, dual hydraulic supply, accumulator) are not tied to this specific mismatch mode. Engineer to characterise the worst-case erroneous response before classifying. NOTE: this condition is not currently present in the SF-008 FCIM.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Braking capability reduced but landing rollout remains within the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement given the ~1,080 m predicted rollout; the operating margin between the two absorbs the degradation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Degraded wheel braking, deceleration still within the landing-distance margin
fha.effCrew: Slight increase in workload to monitor deceleration and stopping distance against the available surface.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: By definition the degradation is contained within the landing-distance margin (~720 m between the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout), so the effect is a slight reduction in safety margin and a slight increase in crew workload — meets the Minor anchor. Remote safety objective applies... [correction: Minor ↔ Probable, 1x10^-3/fh, Part 25]. Engineer to confirm the margin genuinely bounds this partial case for all surface conditions. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Loss of anti-skid on one wheel pair risks wheel lock and tyre burst under braking, particularly on the reduced-friction semi-prepared surface, degrading achieved deceleration and eroding the landing-distance margin.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of anti-skid protection per wheel pair
fha.effCrew: Crew modulate braking manually to avoid lock-up, maintain directional control; increased workload on a surface demanding careful energy management.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The FHA cannot ground the aircraft-level effect of losing anti-skid on a SINGLE wheel pair among twenty tyres without the residual braking/flotation degradation and its effect on the 1,080 m/1,800 m margin — the SDD states anti-skid operates per wheel pair but does not quantify the per-pair contribution. Left empty pending that engineering data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: No wheel braking by any means; deceleration relies on reversers (inboard engines only) and aerodynamic drag. On a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against ~1,080 m predicted rollout the residual means are insufficient to stop within available distance, giving a high-energy overrun onto unprepared terrain.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of wheel braking capability
fha.effCrew: Crew deploy reversers and manage directional control with no braking authority; unable to stop within the strip; excessive workload with an unavoidable overrun.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Complete loss requires the coincident loss of both hydraulic supplies (B normal, A alternate) AND the accumulator reserve sized for six full brake applications, so the true aircraft outcome depends on that residual accumulator braking being also lost — an architecture/exposure question the FHA cannot resolve here. Left empty: effects point toward a severe overrun but classification turns on whether accumulator reserve is credited, which is engineering judgement.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot be directionally controlled on the ground; runway/strip excursion likely on a 1,800 m semi-prepared surface with ~1,080 m rollout margin and no line-maintenance recovery.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants at risk beyond flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground directional control capability (no nose-wheel steering and no differential-braking directional authority)
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to maintain track; high workload attempting recovery with no effective directional means.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of all ground directional authority during takeoff/landing on a narrow semi-prepared strip is a large reduction in safety margins; proposed pending runway-excursion effects analysis and confirmation the outcome is not Catastrophic at high ground speed. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Uncommanded/erroneous steering drives the aircraft off intended track; excursion risk on a narrow semi-prepared strip, potentially at high ground speed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants at risk beyond flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous ground steering response to tiller/pedal command (steers opposite or in excess of command)
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the erroneous response and counter it against the steering input; high workload with limited margin.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An erroneous directional command at ground speed on a narrow strip is a large reduction in safety margins with high crew workload to counter; proposed pending controllability/excursion effects analysis. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants at risk beyond flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Slowly developing steering bias below crew detection threshold
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the function definition does not establish how much lateral track deviation a sub-threshold bias accumulates over the rollout distance, nor whether it results in excursion on the 1,800 m strip. Needs a ground-handling deviation analysis before an aircraft effect and severity can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants at risk beyond flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Degraded ground directional control authority (reduced steering effectiveness)
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the definition establishes that authority is degraded but not the residual controllability or the track-keeping margin remaining on a narrow semi-prepared strip. Needs a controllability determination of the degraded state before an aircraft effect and severity can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants at risk beyond flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of nose-wheel steering with differential-braking directional control retained
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the document confirms braking is a distinct means but does not establish whether differential braking alone provides adequate directional authority on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip. Needs a controllability determination of the differential-braking-only case before an aircraft effect and severity can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Visor departs the pressure boundary / forward-fuselage load path in flight with no prior crew warning; rapid depressurisation of the hold and loss of forward structural integrity; potential loss of the airplane
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants in the hold
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous lock-engaged indication presented with locking pins not driven — visor not actually locked while the flight deck and take-off configuration monitor read locked
fha.effCrew: No indication of the true unlocked state; take-off configuration check falsely satisfied; crew unable to prevent departure of the visor
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous locked indication defeats the take-off configuration check and both dissimilar sensing paths' intent; visor is a single-load-path structure and pressure boundary, so in-flight departure is loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Loss of lock engagement on the ground; visor no longer secured; door cannot be operated in flight per design so condition is confined to ground
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded unlock / latch release with the aircraft on the ground and door otherwise closed
fha.effCrew: Lock status displayed continuously on the flight deck and in the take-off configuration check; crew becomes aware and does not dispatch
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: SDD states the door cannot be operated in flight and lock status is displayed at all times and in the take-off configuration check; an uncommanded ground release is annunciated and caught before dispatch, yielding a slight increase in crew workload. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Visor not fully secured for the pressure boundary / structural load path; take-off configuration monitor reads not-locked and inhibits dispatch
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected
fha.fcDesc: Loss of confirmed lock/latch engagement on closure — closure completes but full latch/pin engagement is not achieved and the shortfall is annunciated

fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Condition is annunciated (lock status displayed and part of the take-off configuration check) and caught on the ground before take-off; effect is a slight increase in crew workload and a dispatch delay, not a reduction in in-flight safety margins. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Blade cannot be loaded or unloaded; no in-flight effect — condition exists only during a ground operation with the aircraft powered from ground supply
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected
fha.fcDesc: Failure to open the nose visor for loading with the door otherwise serviceable
fha.effCrew: Ground crew cannot complete loading; a maintenance/turnaround dispatch issue, no in-flight crew effect

Severity rationale: Opening is a ground operation only and the source states no in-flight effect; inability to open prevents loading (a dispatch/turnaround impact) but produces no effect on the safety of a flight. [anchor NSE-1 — No Safety Effect] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Visor remains correctly locked and the pressure boundary / load path is intact; one of two dissimilar independent lock-confirmation channels is latently unavailable, reducing the assurance of detecting a future unlocked state
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected
fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of lock confirmation on one of the two dissimilar sensing paths, with the door correctly locked
fha.effCrew: Remaining sensing path continues to present lock status; loss of the one channel may itself be undetected so no immediate crew action
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Door remains locked so no immediate hazard; loss of one of two dissimilar sensing paths is a latent reduction in the redundancy of lock confirmation — a slight reduction in safety margins with the fail-safe still intact. Confirm against the fail-safe/latency exposure the engine will evaluate. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Hold cannot be opened for loading/unloading or closed for dispatch; aircraft cannot complete a ground turnaround. Door is not operable in flight so no in-flight aircraft effect arises from this condition.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied and no passengers carried.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose visor open/close capability
fha.effCrew: Ground/loading crew cannot access or secure the hold; dispatch is prevented until the door is restored.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is confined to a ground operation ('cannot be operated in flight'); the SDD does not state an in-flight aircraft-level consequence, so no §25.1309 in-flight safety effect can be derived. Engineer to confirm whether a dispatch/availability-only classification (No Safety Effect for airworthiness) is intended, or whether a mis-secured/partial-close variant is the safety-relevant case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Visor forms the pressure boundary and the forward fuselage structural load path when closed; a false 'locked' indication with lock pins not fully driven could permit pressurisation and take-off with the door not fully secured, risking loss of the pressure boundary and forward load path in flight.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied and no passengers carried.
fha.fcDesc: False indication of locked when not fully locked (crew aware case)
fha.effCrew: Crew rely on flight-deck lock status and the take-off configuration monitor; a false-secure indication removes the cue that would otherwise prevent dispatch.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects support the severe end (loss of pressure boundary / forward structural load path in flight), but the actual outcome depends on whether the dual dissimilar sensing and the take-off configuration monitor catch the mis-lock and on the structural consequence of an in-flight visor release — not established in the SDD. Proposing severity requires the engineer to confirm the credible in-flight outcome (in-flight opening / rapid depressurisation vs. detected-on-ground). Left blank pending that judgement rather than reaching for a class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Flight deck indicates the door is not locked when in fact the lock pins are engaged; nuisance/false-unsafe indication may delay dispatch or prompt an unnecessary reopen attempt. No in-flight loss of the pressure boundary or load path arises because the door is in fact locked.
fha.effPax: None — hold unoccupied and no passengers carried.
fha.fcDesc: False indication of unlocked when actually locked
