fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of heating to a probe or static port
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the heating loss; may act on a degraded or erroneous air-data indication if the affected channel is displayed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a single class: severity turns on whether a single probe/port loss corrupts one channel (voted out by the 3-ADIRU set, likely Major) or can propagate to hazardously misleading displayed data (Hazardous/Catastrophic). The SDD does not state the air-data source-to-display voting/monitoring for a single latent channel loss, so the aircraft effect and thus the class cannot be derived here. Requires the air-data architecture and probe/port-to-channel mapping.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Aircraft remains controllable; attitude, airspeed and altitude presentation retained on primary and independent standby instrument. Navigation solution (position/guidance) degraded or lost.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect other than flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of navigation data with attitude and air data presentation retained
fha.effCrew: Crew fly attitude/air data normally and revert to conventional navigation means; increased workload to navigate and manage the diversion, particularly to a semi-prepared strip with no line maintenance.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot bound the reduction in safety margin without the mission's navigation-dependence at low flight levels and to a semi-prepared strip. SDD gives attitude/air data retention (standby instrument) and dual FMC/nav, but not whether loss of the navigation solution alone yields Minor or Major effect for this operation. Requires engineering input on navigation criticality.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: No direct aircraft-state effect; the alerting system presents a false or mis-prioritised alert. A correct alert may be masked or delayed by mis-prioritisation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect other than flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Spurious or incorrectly prioritised alert presented
fha.effCrew: Crew workload increased managing a spurious or wrongly prioritised alert; potential for a real alert to be missed within the prioritised list, or for an unnecessary crew response to a false condition.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity spans Minor (nuisance workload increase) to Major (mis-prioritisation masking a real condition), and depends on which underlying alert is affected — not enumerable from the function definition alone. The FHA does not yet establish the set of alerts and their criticality needed to bound this. Requires the alert inventory/prioritisation logic to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft state; the aircraft continues to fly. The crew is not annunciated of any system failure or condition, so subsequent failures are not detected and appropriate procedures are not initiated, allowing an otherwise-manageable condition to develop unchecked.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew alerting
fha.effCrew: Crew loses the consolidated prioritised alert list and associated procedures; failures must be inferred from raw parameters, a large increase in workload and a significant reduction in the crew's ability to detect and manage subsequent failures.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of the means by which the crew is told what has failed and what to do removes detection and management of subsequent conditions across all phases; a large reduction in functional capability and excessive crew workload impairing task performance. [anchor HAZ-2 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: No actual fire; if the crew responds to the false warning by shutting down an engine and/or discharging extinguishant, thrust is lost on that engine and, per the SDD, the aircraft is designed to continue following loss of any one engine.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Spurious fire or overheat warning (false alarm)
fha.effCrew: Crew receives a false fire/overheat warning and executes the fire drill (throttle, fuel shut-off, fire handle); increased workload and a diversion decision on a false premise.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A false warning driving an unnecessary engine shutdown produces a significant reduction in functional capability (one engine) and a significant increase in crew workload, but the SDD states one-engine-out continued flight is a design case, keeping it below Hazardous. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: A real engine/APU/bleed/gear-bay fire or overheat exists but is not annunciated; no crew extinguishing action is taken and the fire progresses within the fire zone toward structure, systems and fuel routing, potentially to an uncontrolled fire.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Undetected failure to warn of a real fire or overheat (false negative)
fha.effCrew: Crew is unaware of the fire and continues normal duties; no fire drill is initiated because no warning is presented.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected in-flight fire in a fire zone that receives no extinguishing action removes a safety-margin protection and can progress toward loss of the aircraft; classified Hazardous pending the fire-progression/burn-through argument that would determine whether the unmitigated case is Catastrophic. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Fire/overheat detection is unavailable in one monitored zone (one nacelle, the APU, a bleed run or a gear bay); a fire in that zone alone would not be annunciated while detection in all other zones remains, so protection is lost for one zone only.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of detection in one monitored zone
fha.effCrew: Crew retains alerting for all other zones; a fire in the affected zone would not be presented, so no drill would be initiated for that zone.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft effect depends on whether an undetected fire in the specific unmonitored zone alone drives toward loss of aircraft; the SDD does not state per-zone fire consequence, so the effect cannot be grounded to a class here — needs the zonal fire-hazard argument.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Loss of one detection loop in a zone reverts that zone's warning logic from AND to single-loop per the SDD; warning is retained but the latent state carries a higher exposure to a subsequent undetected loop failure. No immediate aircraft effect while single-loop detection continues to warn.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Degraded dual-loop to single-loop detection logic
fha.effCrew: Crew retains fire/overheat warning for the affected zone on the surviving loop; the degradation is annunciated (a lost loop is a maintenance/dispatch condition), no immediate operational action beyond awareness.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — With warning retained on the surviving loop, this is a latent fault-tolerance reduction rather than a stated aircraft-level effect; classifying it requires the single-loop exposure and combination argument (fault tree / dispatch), not the FHA — left empty rather than assigning No Safety Effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: APU compartment fire cannot be extinguished by its dedicated bottle; automatic APU shutdown and fuel isolation on APU fire remain available; engine extinguishing unaffected.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of APU fire extinguishing only
fha.effCrew: Crew rely on automatic APU shutdown and fuel isolation to manage an APU fire; no extinguishing shot available for the APU compartment.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the SDD: the document states the APU has a dedicated bottle and automatic shutdown/fuel isolation on APU fire, but does not state the aircraft-level consequence of an unextinguished APU fire (structural/adjacent-zone effect) for this configuration. Aircraft effect needed before a severity can be derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Detection continues on a single loop; warning and extinguishing on demand remain available. Reduced detection integrity margin (AND logic lost, single-loop susceptible to spurious or missed indication).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Degraded engine/APU fire extinguishing — detection degraded to single-loop logic on loss of one detection loop
fha.effCrew: Annunciated to crew; single-loop condition is displayed. No immediate action required.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Slight reduction in fire-detection safety margin; extinguishing capability retained and condition annunciated. Grounded in §5.12.2 dual-loop AND logic degrading to single-loop. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: No means to extinguish an engine or APU fire when commanded; a fire, if present, is uncontrolled by the fixed extinguishing system and relies on shutdown/fuel isolation and airframe fire resistance alone.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of engine and APU fire extinguishing on demand
fha.effCrew: Crew commands fire handles with no extinguishant effect; increased workload managing an uncontrollable fire, diversion required.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Large reduction in a functional capability (fire extinguishing) in the presence of a fire; proposed on the conditional-on-fire basis. Grounded in §5.12 fixed extinguishing being the means to suppress engine/APU fire. Engineer to confirm the fire-present combination and whether this reaches Catastrophic for an outboard/wing fire. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Extinguishing unavailable when eventually demanded; latent failure combines with a fire event to produce uncontrolled fire as in the complete-loss case.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Latent unavailability of engine/APU fire extinguishing (bottle pressure lost / discharge circuit failed) — undetected until demand
fha.effCrew: No indication of the latency in normal flight; on demand the fire handle produces no extinguishant. Cylinder pressure is a dispatch item but discharge-circuit latency may not be evident.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Same functional outcome as SF-021-TL but as a latent (unannunciated) unavailability; large reduction in functional capability on demand. Grounded in §5.12; the latency raises exposure-time considerations the engineer should weigh against a Catastrophic combination. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: One of two cylinders lost overboard; crossover valve carries the crew from the remaining cylinder for the required duration at reduced reserve. Thermal discharge indicator shows the event.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded overboard discharge of a cylinder overpressure — loss of one crew-oxygen cylinder supply
fha.effCrew: Reduced oxygen reserve for a subsequent depressurisation/smoke event and diversion; increased workload and dispatch/continuation decision.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in oxygen-supply safety margin (loss of one of two cylinders) with crossover carrying the crew at reduced reserve. Grounded in §5.13.3 crossover carrying the crew at reduced reserve. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Degraded regulator delivery at mask not evident on cylinder pressure until donning
fha.effCrew: Crew donning masks in a depressurisation/smoke/fume event find degraded oxygen delivery not predicted by the cylinder-pressure indication; potential impairment during the very event the system exists to cover.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft-level outcome cannot be grounded: the effect depends on cabin-altitude exposure, diversion time at max operating altitude, and the number of affected mask stations — none stated at aircraft-function level. Regulators are independent per mask (§5.13.3), which bounds the condition to one station, but the severity of degraded delivery during a hypoxia/smoke event is not derivable from the provided material. Engineer to classify with the human-factors/physiology exposure data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Crew oxygen remains available via the crossover from the remaining cylinder; total reserve reduced.
fha.effPax: No effect on occupants — hold unoccupied in flight; no passenger oxygen fitted.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of one cylinder supply (crossover carries crew at reduced reserve)
fha.effCrew: Breathing oxygen still supplied to the crew masks; reduced reserve for the diversion time associated with the maximum operating altitude.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects stated (retained supply via crossover, reduced reserve) cannot be classified without the required diversion-time duration and the margin the reduced reserve leaves against it — the SDD sizes the system 'for four occupants for the diversion time associated with the maximum operating altitude, with reserve' but gives no quantified reserve or duration to judge whether the reduced reserve still meets the requirement. Severity left empty pending that data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Aircraft airworthy; oxygen remains available at the other mask stations.
fha.effPax: No effect on occupants — hold unoccupied in flight; no passenger oxygen fitted.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of oxygen to one mask station only
fha.effCrew: One mask station without oxygen; remaining stations supply the crew. Effect depends on the number of crew on board relative to available stations.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be classified from the function definition alone: severity of losing one of four mask stations depends on the actual crew complement on the affected flight (nominal two, provision for four) and whether a covering station remains for each crew member — the SDD gives the range but not the dispatch complement, so no aircraft effect severity can be derived. Severity left empty pending crew-complement basis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Uncommanded thrust change produces a trajectory/energy deviation; if asymmetric at the 28 m outboard moment arm it induces a yaw/roll excursion the crew must arrest with rudder/aileron within the sizing authority
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change on one or more engines with no crew command
fha.effCrew: Crew detect via engine parameter display and aircraft response, disconnect autothrottle, and manage thrust manually; increased workload
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded asymmetric thrust at the outboard 28 m arm is a large reduction in safety margins / excessive crew workload to arrest the excursion, worst-case at low speed near the ground; crew are aware and act. Confirm against directional-control sizing case. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Symmetric uncommanded thrust change produces an energy/speed and flight-path deviation without a yaw excursion; magnitude depends on the thrust error and phase
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust increase or decrease (symmetric, all-engine or matched)
fha.effCrew: Crew detect via speed/thrust indication, disconnect autothrottle and set thrust manually; increased workload
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect of a SYMMETRIC uncommanded thrust change is not fixed by the function definition alone — severity depends on the magnitude of the thrust error and the phase (e.g. uncommanded loss on take-off vs a small cruise transient). Provide the bounding thrust-error magnitude and worst-case phase to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Loss of one engine yields asymmetric thrust; at the outboard 28 m moment arm this is the directional-control sizing case, requiring rudder authority to hold heading. Aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine at/after V1
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only
fha.fcDesc: Thrust asymmetry from single-engine loss
fha.effCrew: Crew identify the failed engine, apply rudder, secure the engine (fuel shut-off, fire handle) and continue the diversion; significant workload at low speed
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A single-engine loss is within the design dispatch case with continued flight to a suitable aerodrome retained; effect is a significant reduction in margins / significant crew workload rather than a large reduction, since directional authority is sized for this case. Confirm the worst-case (outboard, V1) does not warrant Hazardous once rudder-authority margin is substantiated. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: A slowly developing thrust error accumulates a trajectory/energy or asymmetry deviation while below the crew detection threshold; crew continue duties normally and take no action, so the deviation is uncorrected until it becomes detectable or reaches an envelope limit
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only
fha.fcDesc: Slow thrust drift below the crew detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware by definition; no action taken until the condition crosses a detectable threshold
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect of the UNAWARE drift depends on how far the deviation grows before it becomes detectable and on the asymmetry it develops — the function definition does not bound the endpoint state. Provide the detection threshold and the resulting worst-case deviation/asymmetry at detection to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Aircraft develops an undetected, progressively increasing bank/roll excursion; lateral flight path departs the intended track and, if unarrested, erodes lateral control margins and can progress toward an unusual attitude before recovery is attempted.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded roll developing below the crew detection threshold — a slowly increasing roll rate/bias accumulates without a discrete command and below the level at which the crew perceives or is alerted to it, so no corrective action is taken.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware; on eventual recognition (visual/attitude cue) a high-workload manual recovery from an unexpected attitude is required.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected divergent roll erodes lateral safety margins and forces a high-workload recovery from an unusual attitude — a large reduction in safety margins / functional capabilities. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Loss of the ability to command or arrest bank; the aircraft cannot be maintained on the intended lateral flight path or recovered from a bank excursion — control of the aircraft is lost.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no hold occupants.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of roll control authority — the aircraft can no longer be controlled in the roll axis by any means.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to control the roll axis by any available means.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of a primary flight-control axis prevents control of the aircraft, leading to loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Insufficient pitch authority to control flight path across the required envelope; the aircraft cannot achieve or hold commanded pitch/flight-path in the demanding phases, producing a large reduction in longitudinal safety margins.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no hold occupants.
fha.fcDesc: Degraded pitch control authority outside MAC limits — pitch authority is reduced below the level needed to maintain flight-path control within the manoeuvre/authority envelope.
fha.effCrew: Substantially increased workload to manage flight path with reduced authority; may require limiting the achievable manoeuvre envelope.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Pitch authority insufficient outside MAC limits is a large reduction in functional capability/safety margins in a primary flight-control axis; short of complete loss so not Catastrophic on the stated effects. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Loss of the ability to command or trim pitch; the aircraft cannot maintain or recover flight path in the longitudinal axis — control of the aircraft is lost.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no hold occupants.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of pitch control authority — the aircraft can no longer be controlled in the pitch axis by any means.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to control the pitch axis by any available means, including mechanical reversion.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of a primary flight-control axis prevents control of the aircraft, leading to loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Unintended yaw/sideslip that the crew must counter; on the stated effect it degrades directional control and lateral-directional safety margins, with the worst-case demanding phases (takeoff/landing, engine-out directional case) driving the classification.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no hold occupants.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response to crew command — the yaw axis responds differently from the crew's command (wrong sense or wrong magnitude), producing an unintended yaw/sideslip.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the mismatched yaw response and counter it, increasing workload; effect severity depends on onset magnitude and phase.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous yaw response degrades directional control margins consistent with the SF-005 malfunction family (yaw jam/erroneous cases classified Hazardous); however the function definition does not bound response magnitude, so the committed class is the worst credible on the stated effects — engineer to confirm the bound. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Fuselage differential driven above the scheduled value; independent positive-pressure relief valves protect structure regardless of the control system, capping over-differential below a structurally damaging level.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous cabin differential above scheduled value
fha.effCrew: Erroneous/high-differential indication and alerting; crew reverts to manual/pneumatic backup mode and manages descent — increased workload.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Structure protected by independent mechanical relief (positive relief valves), bounding the effect to a significant increase in crew workload and reduced margins rather than structural failure. Confirm the scheduled-value margin and relief setting — hold differential is preliminary. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: First extinguishing attempt against an actual engine fire is misdirected; the burning nacelle receives no agent on that discharge. Second bottle of the pair (cross-plumbed) remains available for a correct discharge, so extinguishing capability is not exhausted.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Extinguishant discharge into wrong nacelle of the pair — agent delivered to a non-burning nacelle while the affected nacelle receives none on the first shot
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the misdirected discharge and command the remaining bottle; increased workload during a fire event.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of the first extinguishing attempt against an actual fire with one correct discharge still available; significant reduction in a safety function with increased crew workload. Severity is conditional on a concurrent real fire — see assumption. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Extinguishing to the affected nacelle is reduced from two available shots to one; the dedicated bottle can still discharge directly. Reduction in fire-suppression margin for that nacelle.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of extinguishing to one nacelle of a pair — cross-plumb path unavailable; only the dedicated single-shot discharge to that nacelle remains
fha.effCrew: Single discharge available for that nacelle; crew has one attempt rather than a backup shot.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-shot extinguishing retained to the affected nacelle rather than complete loss; a significant reduction in the fire-protection margin. Severity is conditional on a concurrent real fire — see assumption. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: No aircraft handling effect directly; the aircraft remains controllable.
fha.effPax: No passengers; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew breathing oxygen supply — no oxygen delivered to any mask station
fha.effCrew: No breathing oxygen available for a depressurisation, smoke or fume event; in a smoke/fume event the flight crew have no protective supply for the descent and diversion the system is sized for. Flight crew are the only occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of the crew's protective oxygen removes the mitigation for a smoke/fume or depressurisation event, exposing the only occupants (flight crew) — a large reduction in safety margin. Governing event (smoke/fume vs depressurisation at FL260) determines the exact class; left open pending crew-effect judgement. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Loss of thrust on one side produces a yawing/rolling moment about the 28 m outboard moment arm that the flight-crew must counter with rudder; the aircraft continues to a suitable aerodrome on the remaining engines, as designed for one-engine loss at or after V1, with reduced climb performance and asymmetric trim.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of propulsive thrust — asymmetric, one side, within available directional-control authority
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to trim and maintain directional control and to manage the affected engine (fuel shut-off, fire handle if required); significant reduction in performance margins on take-off/climb.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Asymmetric partial thrust loss within the available directional-control authority is a significant reduction in performance margins with a significant increase in crew workload; the aircraft is designed to continue on remaining engines. Severe cases (outside available authority / second engine same side) are captured separately in SF-001-PL2. Engineer to confirm against the flight-control directional-control sizing case. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: An uncommanded yaw input imposes sideslip and a coupled roll; at the low-speed/high-workload phases (take-off, approach, landing) it degrades tracking and, if of sufficient magnitude, reduces safety margins toward controllability limits before the crew arrests it.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw motion with no crew command
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the departure, apply corrective pedal/inceptor input and diagnose the source; increased workload with a reduction in directional safety margins.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded, crew-aware yaw departure at a critical phase is a large reduction in safety margins requiring prompt corrective action; classed Hazardous by analogy to the yaw-authority-loss-outside-limits condition (SF-005-PL2). Magnitude of the achievable uncommanded deflection is not stated in the SDD — engineer to confirm the class against the split-rudder single-segment authority. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Reduced deceleration extends the landing rollout from the predicted ~1,080 m toward the 1,800 m requirement, consuming the operating margin on the semi-prepared strip; if degradation is sufficient the aircraft cannot stop within the available distance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Degraded wheel braking eroding into the landing-distance margin
fha.effCrew: Crew is aware of degraded braking (reduced deceleration / anti-skid or brake status), must maximise braking, use reverse thrust on the inboard engines and manage the rollout; increased workload with reduced stopping margin.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erosion of the 1,800 m vs ~1,080 m landing margin with the crew aware is a significant reduction in safety margins; classed Major provided sufficient margin/reverse remains to stop on the strip. If degradation can consume the full margin (overrun on a semi-prepared surface) the class rises — engineer to confirm the deceleration threshold at which the margin is exhausted. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Braking capability is reduced but the shortfall is not annunciated; the crew continue normal duties and apply nominal braking, so the reduced deceleration is only revealed by the rollout failing to develop as predicted — potentially too late to recover the landing-distance margin on the 1,800 m strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Undetected braking degradation below the crew detection threshold
fha.effCrew: Crew take no corrective action for the degradation because it is below the detection threshold; they fly the expected stopping performance and discover the shortfall during rollout.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Crew-unaware case: the aircraft-level effect depends on how much undetected deceleration shortfall can accumulate before the ~1,080 m predicted rollout exceeds the 1,800 m requirement, and the SDD does not state a detection threshold or the deceleration value at which the margin is exhausted. Cannot classify without that data — engineer to establish the undetected-degradation magnitude and its rollout consequence.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: An uncommanded nose-wheel steering deflection introduces a directional excursion during the ground run; at take-off/landing speeds this can drive the aircraft off the semi-prepared strip centreline before the crew counters it with differential braking and pedal steering.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded ground steering deflection without crew command
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded deflection and arrest the excursion with steering/differential braking; increased workload with reduced directional margin on a narrow semi-prepared surface.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded ground steering deflection at speed is a large reduction in directional safety margins with risk of a runway/strip excursion; classed Hazardous by analogy to the erroneous ground-steering condition (SF-009-M2, Hazardous). Magnitude of the achievable uncommanded deflection is not stated — engineer to confirm against the steering actuator authority. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Primary display presentation of flight and navigation data is lost across all display units; crew reverts to the independent integrated standby instrument (attitude, airspeed, altitude) which shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries. Navigation and situational data beyond the standby set are unavailable; capability to continue safe flight and landing is significantly reduced, particularly in IMC in the low flight levels.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight and navigation data presentation
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effCrew: Large increase in workload flying on standby instrumentation alone with loss of navigation and consolidated situational information; degraded ability to manage the aircraft in IMC.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of primary flight/nav presentation with only the standby instrument surviving is a large reduction in functional capabilities and a large increase in crew workload; effects support Hazardous. NOT Catastrophic because the SDD states the standby instrument shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries and remains available — engineer to confirm that independence claim; if the standby is not credible in this condition the class rises. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: The alerting system fails to present an alert for a real condition; the underlying failure progresses without crew action because the aircraft's single consolidated crew alert list is the means by which the crew is told what has failed and what to do. Undetected, the unannunciated condition may develop into a more severe aircraft state before it becomes evident by other means.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.fcDesc: Missing or suppressed alert for a real condition (silent alerting failure), crew unaware
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally and take no action regarding the unannunciated condition; recovery is delayed until the effect becomes apparent independently, by which point safety margins may be reduced.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity of a silent (crew-unaware) alerting failure depends on the severity of the specific underlying condition left unannunciated and on what other independent cues exist — the alerting function's definition alone does not fix an aircraft effect for the suppressed alert. Cannot derive a class without that mapping; engineer to assess the worst-credible unannunciated condition.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: One of the two independent alerting processing channels is lost; the remaining channel continues to consolidate and present the crew alert list, so alerting capability is retained with reduced redundancy. Loss is annunciated.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of one alerting processing channel
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effCrew: Slight increase in workload/awareness of the degraded configuration; alerting remains available through the second channel with no immediate operational limitation.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With the second independent alerting channel retained and the loss annunciated, the condition is at most a slight reduction in redundancy with alerting still fully available — effects support Minor. Rests on the SDD claim of two independent processing channels; engineer to confirm the surviving channel is fully capable. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Detection of fire and overheat is lost across the monitored zones (engine nacelles, APU, bleed duct runs, main gear bays, hold smoke stations); a fire or overheat could develop and progress without warning to the crew. Extinguishing means remain but cannot be applied in time without detection. Undetected fire in a fire zone is a potential loss-of-aircraft precursor.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normally with no annunciation of a developing fire/overheat; no timely opportunity to actuate fire handles or take avoiding action.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of fire/overheat detection removes the warning on which timely crew fire response depends; a developing fire could reach a serious aircraft state before becoming evident, a large reduction in safety margins. Proposed Hazardous. Could be argued Catastrophic if an undetected engine/APU fire is judged unsurvivable in the worst phase — engineer to assess against the dual-loop, multi-zone architecture and whether all detection is credibly lost simultaneously. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: An extinguisher bottle discharges into a nacelle (or APU) with no fire present; extinguishing agent for that engine pair is consumed and unavailable for a subsequent genuine fire, given two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed. No direct effect on thrust or aircraft control from the discharge itself; the condition is a latent reduction in fire-suppression capability plus crew distraction from the associated warning/handle activity.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguishant discharge with no fire
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effCrew: Crew workload increase to diagnose the spurious discharge and confirm no fire; management of the now-reduced extinguishing reserve for that engine pair.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Inadvertent discharge with no fire does not directly affect flight capability; its consequence is reduced extinguishing reserve (second bottle per pair remains, cross-plumbed) and a slight workload increase — effects support Minor. Rests on there being no adverse effect of the agent on the engine and on a second bottle remaining; engineer to confirm the cross-plumbed reserve and any engine impact. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Air conditioning and distribution continues from a single source at a reduced schedule; conditioning margin reduced.
fha.fcDesc: Reduced conditioning schedule on single-source air
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive an aircraft effect: the function definition and SDD do not state whether a reduced single-source conditioning schedule breaches a flight-deck environment or pressurisation-supply limit. Hold is unoccupied in flight, so occupant effect is not the driver. Needs engineering judgement on flight-deck conditioning adequacy before a class is committed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: No heating to probes, static ports and windshields and no ice detection; probes and ports subject to icing with no advisory of accretion.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of probe heating and ice detection
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive an aircraft effect from the function definition alone: the consequence of losing probe heating (potential unreliable airspeed/altitude/attitude to the air data references) and the icing exposure over which it acts are not stated. Needs engineering judgement on air-data integrity and icing-envelope exposure before a class is committed.. Engineer to classify.

assumptions.text: The four systems FUE, HYD, EPS and EWS are resources and are excluded from aircraft-function authoring; the behaviours their consumers accomplish are captured instead.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any resource must be modelled as a function, additional aircraft functions (e.g. distribute electrical power) would be added and consumer traces would change.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS from the function list; all 9 authored top functions.

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft themselves

assumptions.rationale: The SDD's own inventory classes these as resources rather than functions, and the modeling rule bars authoring resources as functions.

assumptions.text: The nose visor structural load path and the hold floor hard-points are structure, not functions; only the door open/close/lock behaviour and the restraint behaviour are authored.
assumptions.ifWrong: If structural integrity is to be tracked as a functional-FHA item, that would incorrectly duplicate PRA/structural analysis scope.
assumptions.usedFor: Provide hold access and closure; Restrain payload sub-functions.

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly states the door is a single load path treated as structure and hold hard-points have no redundancy.

assumptions.text: Roll spoilers are captured within the roll control sub-function rather than split out as an independent speed-brake/lift-dump behaviour.
assumptions.ifWrong: A separate 'provide lift dump / speed brake' aircraft function may be warranted, changing the deceleration and roll decomposition.

citations.quote: Roll is by two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers

assumptions.rationale: The SDD groups spoilers with ailerons under roll and does not describe an independent ground-lift-dump function; §6 omitted routing chapters may bear on independence.

assumptions.text: The mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim and lower rudder segment leaves a survivable degraded control mode after loss of all three flight control computers, so pitch/yaw total-loss is split into within-MAC and outside-MAC partials rather than a single unrecoverable total loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reversion authority is insufficient, the outside-MAC partial for SF-004/SF-005 collapses into a full total-loss condition and the AFHA severity anchoring changes.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004 and SF-005 partials[] within/outside-MAC entries

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only, providing a survivable but degraded means of control

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states a mechanical reversion exists but does not quantify the residual authority, so I cannot ground whether the outside-MAC partial is truly unrecoverable.

assumptions.text: Directional-control authority limits the acceptable single-side thrust asymmetry, so asymmetric thrust is a distinct SF-001 failure condition separate from symmetric total loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: If asymmetric thrust is fully controllable at all times, the outside-authority partial for SF-001 disappears and rolls up differently in the AFHA.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001 partials[] asymmetric entries and malfunctions[] thrust-asymmetry entry

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names the outboard-engine asymmetric case as the sizing case for directional control but does not fix the authority boundary, so the within/outside-authority split is preliminary.

assumptions.text: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by WoW and radio-altimeter agreement plus a mechanical sleeve lock, so in-flight inadvertent deployment is retained as a low-likelihood malfunction condition rather than dismissed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the inhibit is shown fully independent and dependable, the in-flight-deployment SF-002 malfunction may be dispositioned out of the AFHA.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002 malfunction 'inadvertent reverse thrust deployment in flight'

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes inhibits but the FCIM must still carry the erroneous-provision malfunction until the AFHA/SFHA substantiate the inhibit integrity.

assumptions.text: Combined-condition candidate: simultaneous partial loss of yaw control (single rudder supply loss) with an outboard-engine thrust asymmetry is the directional sizing case and should be filed in the matrix Combined column for SF-005 x SF-001.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the combined case is not credible, the Combined-column entry is dropped and rudder-authority requirements are not driven by it.

citations.quote: a single rudder supply loss must still leave sufficient authority

assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly ties the split-rudder arrangement to the engine-out-plus-blade-payload case, which is a combined failure condition A3 requires me to flag.

assumptions.text: Crew-unaware rows carry only conditions that can develop below detection thresholds (slow drift/bias); the SDD gives no alerting or detection detail for these, so indication/mitigation fields are left empty pending AFHA effects.
assumptions.ifWrong: If alerting exists for these drift conditions, the unaware rows may collapse into the Aware rows and indication fields get populated.
assumptions.usedFor: All Unaware rows for SF-001, SF-003, SF-004, SF-005
assumptions.rationale: No alerting or crew-detection means for slow control-axis or thrust drift is described in the extracted sections, so awareness cues cannot be grounded.

assumptions.text: High-lift asymmetry is annunciated to the crew via the asymmetry brakes / jam discretes, making the asymmetric and erroneous-response conditions crew-Aware.
assumptions.ifWrong: If asymmetry is not annunciated, the SF-006 asymmetric-deployment condition moves to the crew-Unaware row and the mitigation/indication fields must change.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006 Aware malfunctions row (asymmetric deployment / erroneous response)

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes; high-lift position to the performance computation.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names asymmetry brakes and jam discretes but does not explicitly state a crew alert, forcing the awareness assignment.

assumptions.text: Braking degradation is perceptible relative to the ~1,080 m predicted rollout against the 1,800 m requirement, so degraded-braking conditions are crew-Aware in normal cases but a low-level erosion can develop undetected.
assumptions.ifWrong: If degradation is not indicated, the SF-008 degraded rows consolidate onto the Unaware row and mitigation credit changes.

citations.quote: predicted landing rollout is approximately 1,080 m, and the margin between the two

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the distance margin and brake-temperature monitoring but no explicit degraded-braking alert, forcing the aware/unaware split.

assumptions.text: The nose visor cannot be operated in flight, so its erroneous-open / uncommanded-unlock malfunction is a ground condition, while lock-status indication is continuously available in flight.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an in-flight unlock path exists, an in-flight loss-of-pressure-boundary malfunction condition must be added to SF-010.

citations.quote: is operated from a ground handling panel ... and cannot be operated in flight

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the door cannot be operated in flight and lock status is displayed continuously, bounding which SF-010 conditions are flight vs ground.

assumptions.text: The dual dissimilar nose-door sensing paths make single-path loss detectable via disagreement, so the undetected case applies only to a single sensing path, not both.
assumptions.ifWrong: If disagreement is not annunciated, the SF-010 erroneous-lock-indication condition becomes fully crew-Unaware and its mitigation credit is lost.

citations.quote: two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes dual dissimilar independently-routed sensing but does not state disagreement alerting, forcing the per-condition unaware framing.

assumptions.text: Loss of nose-wheel steering leaves residual ground directional control via differential braking, supporting the SF-009 partial-loss condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If differential braking is not usable for steering, the SF-009 partial-loss condition is invalid and only complete loss remains for steering failures.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-009 partial (steering lost, differential braking retained)

citations.quote: provides braking and directional control on the ground

assumptions.rationale: Steering and braking are distinct per the SDD but the SDD does not explicitly state differential braking is a directional-control fallback, forcing this assumption.

assumptions.text: The crew-Aware split for SF-011/012/013/015 rests on the SDD's stated annunciations being active and correctly calibrated in flight.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an annunciation is absent or inhibited in the relevant phase, the affected condition moves to the crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011 Aware/Unaware, SF-012 Aware, SF-013 Aware, SF-015 Aware rows

citations.quote: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight

assumptions.rationale: The FCIM awareness tag requires knowing detection means; the function list alone cannot confirm the alert reaches the crew in the relevant phase.

assumptions.text: SF-014 conditioning-loss detection is not clearly grounded, so its unaware malfunction row is left with empty indication/mitigation fields.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a conditioning fault annunciation exists, the SF-014 unaware malfunction may reclassify to Aware and gain an indication field.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes air distribution and single-pack schedules but does not state a discrete conditioning-failure annunciation to the crew.

assumptions.text: SF-011 lock loss and SF-015 pressurisation form a combined pressure-boundary-integrity condition via the nose door interlock.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the interlock fully decouples the two, no combined condition is warranted and the Combined-column flag is dropped.

citations.quote: a pressure interlock vents and confirms residual differential below 0.1 psi before the lock actuator will run

assumptions.rationale: The FCIM Combined column needs cross-function coupling identified; the interlock ties door lock state to pressurisation.

assumptions.text: A lost ice-protection zone is annunciated but an undetected silent loss of a single zone remains possible where the annunciation path itself fails.
assumptions.ifWrong: If every protection loss is annunciated, the SF-016 crew-unaware row collapses to N/A.

citations.quote: Electrical zones are independently supplied and a lost zone is annunciated.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD grounds annunciation of a lost electrical zone but does not state monitoring coverage for every bleed-protected surface, forcing the SF-016 unaware row.

assumptions.text: The two identical ice detectors share a common-mode false-negative susceptibility that can suppress accretion detection undetected.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detector dissimilarity or an independent cross-check is confirmed, the SF-017 undetected false-negative malfunction is removed.

citations.quote: The two ice detectors are identical in type and their commonality is recorded as an item for examination.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD records detector commonality as an open item rather than an independence claim, forcing the SF-017 unaware false-negative condition.

assumptions.text: Erroneous flight/navigation data can present common-mode across the three reference units without a disagreement flag, making an HMI condition crew-unaware.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a cross-comparison monitor always flags common-mode error, the SF-018 undetected HMI malfunction becomes crew-aware.

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states three reference units and a standby but does not confirm a monitor that catches a plausible common-mode error, forcing the SF-018 unaware HMI condition.

assumptions.text: Loss of crew alerting (SF-019) combined with loss of the detection it presents (SF-020) is a related-sub-function combined failure condition to be carried in the matrix's Combined column.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detection annunciation is independent of the consolidated alerting channel, no combined SF-019/SF-020 condition is needed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019 / SF-020 combined condition (engineer files in Combined column)

citations.quote: Fire and overheat warnings to the crew alerting system

assumptions.rationale: SF-020 detection feeds the SF-019 alerting list; the ARP4761A A3 combined-condition text requires flagging such coupled losses, which single-function rows cannot capture.

assumptions.text: Loss of engine/APU fire extinguishing is only consequential in coincidence with an actual fire event, so it is treated as a combined condition against a live fire.
assumptions.ifWrong: If extinguishing loss is consequential without a coincident fire, the SF-021 Total-loss condition would stand alone rather than needing the Combined column.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-021 Total loss / Unaware latent-loss rows

citations.quote: provides the means to extinguish or suppress them

assumptions.rationale: The function list gives the extinguishing capability alone; the SDD describes detection and discharge but the FCIM cannot classify the standalone loss without the coincident fire that makes it matter.

assumptions.text: Latent unavailability of the extinguisher discharge (lost bottle pressure or open discharge circuit) is not annunciated until the fire handle is pulled.
assumptions.ifWrong: If bottle/discharge readiness is continuously monitored and annunciated, the SF-021 Unaware row collapses into the Aware row.

citations.quote: Two extinguisher bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed so that either bottle can discharge into either nacelle

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states discharge is hot-battery supplied and crew-commanded but does not describe continuous monitoring or built-in test of bottle readiness, so undetectable latency cannot be excluded.

assumptions.text: A degraded per-mask regulator delivery fault does not register on the displayed cylinder pressure and is therefore not evident until the mask is donned.
assumptions.ifWrong: If per-mask delivery is monitored and alerted, the SF-022 Unaware malfunction row moves to the Aware row.

citations.quote: Regulators are independent per mask.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD grounds continuous cylinder-pressure display and low-pressure alerting but describes no per-mask delivery monitoring, so a downstream regulator malfunction can develop below the pressure indication.

assumptions.text: Loss of crew oxygen delivery is the driving condition specifically in coincidence with depressurisation, smoke or fume events.
assumptions.ifWrong: If oxygen loss is consequential outside those demand cases, the SF-022 Total-loss condition stands alone without the Combined column entry.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022 Total loss row / Combined column flag

citations.quote: supplies breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names those as the demand cases; the function list alone does not state the coincident driver, so the combined pairing is flagged rather than merged into a single FCIM cell.

assumptions.text: Directional control sized to the outboard-engine-out asymmetry bounds the single-engine and one-side partial-loss thrust conditions at Hazardous rather than Catastrophic.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the sizing case does not leave adequate control authority, SF-001-M2, M3 and PL would move toward Catastrophic (CAT-1).

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names the outboard-engine-out case as the sizing case but does not quantify residual controllability margin, so the boundary between HAZ and CAT is not established in the inputs.

assumptions.text: Loss of a second engine on the same side is a separate, higher-severity condition and is not covered by the SF-001 rows this turn.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the two-engine case must be captured under SF-001-PL, that row understates severity and a distinct Catastrophic-candidate row is required.

citations.quote: Loss of a second engine on the same side is outside the design dispatch case and is retained as a condition to be studied

assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly places two-engines-same-side outside the design dispatch case, but the FCIM did not list it as a distinct SF-001 condition.

assumptions.text: The slow sub-threshold thrust drift (SF-001-M4) becomes detectable and correctable before it develops into a large asymmetry.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the drift can grow undetected into an uncontrollable asymmetry, SF-001-M4 rises from Major toward Hazardous or Catastrophic.

citations.quote: slow thrust drift below crew detection threshold

assumptions.rationale: The FCIM defines the condition as below the crew detection threshold but the inputs do not state how or when it eventually manifests, forcing an assumption about its endpoint to classify it.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the only occupants are flight crew, so passenger effects are not a severity driver.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants are ever carried, passenger-effect columns and severity floors for SF-001 conditions change.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax for all five SF-001 rows

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: The FHA needs an occupant-effect statement; the SDD states the hold is not occupied and the aircraft carries flight crew only.

assumptions.text: The flight hold is unoccupied in flight, so passenger effects are not applicable to any of these conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in the hold, the occupant-effect column and possibly the severity of the loss/asymmetry conditions would change.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on SF-001-PL2, SF-001-TL, SF-002-M, SF-002-M2, SF-002-M3

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: The FHA requires an occupant-effect entry; the provided text states the hold is not occupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only.

assumptions.text: An asymmetric thrust condition exceeding the sized rudder authority results in loss of controlled flight.
assumptions.ifWrong: If residual controllability exists beyond the sized authority, SF-001-PL2 and SF-002-M could be Hazardous rather than Catastrophic.

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names the outboard-engine asymmetry at the 28 m arm as the directional-control sizing case but does not itself state the controllability outcome when that authority is exceeded.

assumptions.text: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only, so reverser conditions concern inboard-engine reverse thrust.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reversers were fitted differently, the asymmetry magnitude and stopping-contribution effects for SF-002 rows would change.

citations.quote: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only.

assumptions.rationale: Effect statements for SF-002 conditions depend on which engines provide reverse thrust; the SDD specifies inboard-only.

assumptions.text: Reverse thrust is a supplementary, non-credited contributor to landing deceleration, with wheel braking and flotation carrying the certified stopping performance.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reverse thrust is credited landing distance, SF-002-TL loss could reduce the safety margin more severely (potentially Hazardous) and SF-002-PL would become classifiable and non-trivial.

citations.quote: The margin between those two numbers is the operating margin on which the braking and flotation design rests.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the requirement/predicted-rollout margin 'is the operating margin on which the braking and flotation design rests' but does not state whether reverse-thrust distance is credited, so a severity for loss of reverse thrust must assume the credit basis.

assumptions.text: The SF-002 partial/total reverse-thrust conditions are ground-only (deployment inhibited in flight), so no in-flight failure effect is assessed for these rows.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the ground scoping is incorrect the phase set and effects for SF-002 rows would need an in-flight case added.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-PL and SF-002-TL phases (Landing rollout) and effects

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement

assumptions.rationale: The failure conditions are stated as 'on ground' and the SDD inhibits reverse deployment in flight; inadvertent in-flight deployment is a separate malfunction condition not in this turn's list.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight so all three SF-003 roll-malfunction rows carry no passenger/occupant effect.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants are carried, the occupant-effect column and potentially the severity of the roll malfunctions would change.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on SF-003-M, SF-003-M2, SF-003-M3 and SF-002 rows

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: Occupant effect is a required FHA column; the SDD states the hold is not occupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only.

assumptions.text: "MAC limits" in the FCIM cell text denotes a manoeuvre/authority (control-authority) envelope, such that degradation within it leaves the aircraft controllable and degradation outside it does not.
assumptions.ifWrong: If "MAC" means something else (e.g. mean aerodynamic chord CG reference) the PL/PL2 split and their Minor/Hazardous classifications would be re-scoped or merged.

assumptions.rationale: The provided FCIM condition text uses "within MAC limits" / "outside MAC limits" without defining MAC; the SDD does not define this term, so the boundary distinguishing PL from PL2 severity had to be interpreted.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only, so no passenger-effect exists for any SF-003 condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants are ever carried in flight, every SF-003 row would need a passenger-effect assessment and severities for degradation/loss cases could rise.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax for SF-003-M4, SF-003-M5, SF-003-PL, SF-003-PL2, SF-003-TL

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: The occupant effect column requires knowing who is aboard; the SDD states the hold is not occupied in flight and the crew complement is flight crew only.

assumptions.ifWrong: If yaw contributors should be developed in this tree, the AND gate's right branch expands into rudder-segment/hydraulic-supply basic events, deepening the tree.

citations.quote: a single rudder supply loss must still leave sufficient authority

assumptions.text: The 3-way FCC vote/comparator provides monitoring coverage that must fail concurrently with a single FCC error for an erroneous or uncommanded command to reach the surfaces.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the computers vote on command but does not describe the monitor's detection coverage, forcing an AND between a bad FCC output and a monitor non-detection.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the vote does not isolate a single bad output, the FCC contributor becomes an order-1 (single-point) input under the OR gate rather than an AND, changing the tree structure and single-point-failure flag.
assumptions.usedFor: AND gates under SF-004-M and SF-004-M2

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.text: The three flight control computers are independent (separate bays, separate electrical sources) so a single common cause does not defeat the vote.
assumptions.rationale: Independence is claimed by installation in three separate bays and supply from three different electrical sources, but common-cause has not been assessed here.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a common cause defeats the vote, the FCC AND gate collapses toward a single point and the trees for both conditions must add a common-cause basic event.
assumptions.usedFor: FCC AND-gate inputs under SF-004-M and SF-004-M2

citations.quote: Each computer is supplied from a different electrical source

assumptions.text: FCC and ACE internal architecture is the resolution limit; no deeper basic events are modelled because the SDD does not resolve their internals.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes FCCs and actuator control electronics as blocks without sub-structure, so decomposing further would fabricate depth.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a lower-level FCC/ACE architecture is later provided, the corresponding basic events split into sub-trees.
assumptions.usedFor: Leaf basic events for FCC and ACE in both trees

citations.quote: electrical power to the computers and to the actuator control electronics

assumptions.text: A stabiliser trim runaway is arrested by a monitor/automatic cutout or crew action that is a distinct contributor from the erroneous drive itself.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes a mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim but does not state any trim-runaway monitoring or cutout logic, so the arrest mechanism is assumed rather than read.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-004-M3 trim-runaway branch AND gate collapses toward a single-event OR, changing the tree structure and any SPF finding.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-M3 gate 'Stabiliser trim runaway to extreme' and its 'Failure to detect and arrest trim runaway' input

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.text: The three dissimilar FCCs form an independent command contributor to elevator loss such that all three command paths must be lost for elevator command loss.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states three dissimilar computers on three separate electrical sources but does not confirm that every elevator actuator control path draws on all three, so the AND across FCC 1/2/3 is inferred.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single FCC or shared actuator-control-electronics feeds the elevators, the FCC branch becomes a lower-order cut set and SF-004-TL may expose a nearer single/dual point of failure.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-TL gate 'Loss of FCC command to elevator actuators'

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command. Each computer is supplied from a different electrical source

assumptions.text: Elevators are driven by hydraulic systems A and C only, so loss of both A and C removes powered elevator authority.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD assigns 'the elevators from A and C'; the tree's dual-supply AND for elevator loss rests directly on that allocation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an additional supply or a shared A/C dependency exists, the elevator-loss AND gate order changes and the independence claim in SF-004-TL is affected.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-TL gate 'Loss of elevator control' A and C branches; SF-004-M3 elevator actuator inputs

citations.quote: the elevators from A and C; the ailerons from B and C

assumptions.text: The upper rudder segment is supplied by HYD A and the lower segment by HYD B.
assumptions.rationale: §5.3.2 states each segment has its own hydraulic supply but the A/B-to-segment mapping is only given in the §2.2 interface line 'A → rudder upper, elevators; B → rudder lower, ailerons'.
assumptions.ifWrong: The specific hydraulic-loss basic events under each SF-005-TL segment branch swap systems; gate logic (AND of two segments) is unchanged.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-TL nodes 'Loss of HYD A supply to upper rudder' and 'Loss of HYD B supply to lower rudder'

citations.quote: A → rudder upper, elevators; B → rudder lower, ailerons

assumptions.text: The mechanical reversion path backs up only the lower rudder segment, so upper-segment command loss has no mechanical backstop.
assumptions.rationale: §5.3.2 states the mechanical reversion path exists 'to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only'.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reversion also serves the upper segment, the upper command-loss branch becomes an AND (FBW + reversion) rather than a single OR input.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-TL asymmetry between upper (OR command) and lower (AND command) branches

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.text: 'Below detection threshold' for SF-006-M3 means the asymmetry-detection and asymmetry-brake protection must also fail (or not act) for the condition to exist.
assumptions.rationale: The FC is defined as below the detection threshold; the SDD provides asymmetry brakes and asymmetry/jam discretes as the protection, so the undetected condition requires that protection to fail to arrest/annunciate.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the detection layer is not credited, the top event reduces to an OR of the asymmetry mechanisms alone and the protective AND branch is removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006-M3 top AND gate and its 'protection fails to detect/arrest' branch

citations.quote: through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section

assumptions.text: Complete loss of ground support at touchdown is dominated by failure to reach a locked-down gear configuration and by gear structural collapse, with no other credible top contributor.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes extension/lockdown and treats gear structure as non-redundant, but does not enumerate touchdown-load failure modes, forcing a two-branch model.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a third independent contributor exists (e.g. bogie tyre/flotation failure driving loss of support), the SF-007-TL OR gate gains a branch.

citations.quote: One twin-wheel steerable nose unit and six three-wheel main bogies, three per side

assumptions.text: The free-fall alternate extension is genuinely independent of HYD system A, so both must fail for gear not to reach lockdown.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states free-fall is an alternate to HYD-A extension but does not detail its actuation independence.
assumptions.ifWrong: If free-fall shares a failure source with HYD-A extension, the AND collapses toward a single-point path and SF-007-TL loses its independence claim.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-007-TL 'Gear not in locked-down configuration' AND gate

citations.quote: free-fall extension independent of hydraulic pressure

assumptions.text: The two dissimilar lock-sensing channels are independent, so a false 'locked' indication requires BOTH channels to fail false while pins are not driven.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD claims dissimilar and independently routed sensing but this independence is asserted, not substantiated.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a common cause defeats both channels, the SF-010-M sensing AND collapses to an OR and the condition becomes near single-point.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-010-M 'Both dissimilar sensing channels falsely indicate locked' AND gate

citations.quote: a proximity sensing harness reading pin position directly, and a mechanical linkage driving a visual indicator

assumptions.text: The pin actuator and its separate hydraulic supply resolve no deeper than actuator/supply-level basic events for this pass.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply but does not decompose its internal fault modes.
assumptions.ifWrong: If piece-part resolution is required, the pins-not-driven OR branch expands with additional basic events.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-010-M 'Locking pins not driven' OR gate

citations.quote: Eight independent locking pins are then driven through the latch bodies by a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply

assumptions.text: The common torque shaft driving all twelve latches is a single element whose failure defeats the entire latch set.
assumptions.rationale: SDD states the twelve rotary latches are 'driven by a common torque shaft' but does not decompose the shaft into segments or state any redundancy in it.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the torque shaft is segmented/redundant, the 'Common torque shaft failure' order-1 event should be replaced by an AND across segments, changing the latch branch structure.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011-TL latch-set OR branch, basic event 'Common torque shaft failure (all twelve latches)'

citations.quote: Twelve rotary latches engage on closure, driven by a common torque shaft.

assumptions.text: The locking pins are engaged by a single lock actuator on a single (separate) hydraulic supply, distinct from the latch drive.
assumptions.rationale: SDD says eight pins are 'driven through the latch bodies by a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply' but does not state whether the pin actuator itself is redundant.
assumptions.ifWrong: If pin actuation is redundant, the pin OR branch understates margin; if the pin supply shares a source with the latch drive, the engagement AND collapses toward order-1.

citations.quote: Eight independent locking pins are then driven through the latch bodies by a separate actuator on a separate hydraulic supply

assumptions.text: Loss of longitudinal restraint at one station requires loss of BOTH straps at that station OR loss of the station's single saddle-to-hardpoint load path.
assumptions.rationale: SDD gives two straps per saddle and states 'no redundancy in the hold floor hard points'; the FC is single-station loss so both-strap failure plus the shared hardpoint are the contributors.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single strap loss alone constitutes 'loss of longitudinal restraint at one station' the top gate becomes an OR of single straps, making each strap an order-1 cut set.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012-PL top-gate structure and both-strap AND

citations.quote: load paths sized such that the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours. There is no redundancy in the hold floor hard points

assumptions.text: The two lock-confirmation channels (proximity harness and mechanical linkage/indicator) are independent and both must fail for confirmation to be lost.
assumptions.rationale: SDD describes the two circuits as 'dissimilar and independently routed'; independence is asserted in the design and must be verified, not assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the two channels share a route or penetration, the confirmation AND becomes a common-cause candidate and the branch weakens toward order-1.

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.text: Complete loss of restraint requires either failure of the shared hold-floor hard-point load path or simultaneous loss of both straps and saddle geometry at effectively every station.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes redundancy such that one strap loss is carried by neighbours, so a whole-payload restraint loss is only reached by the common attachment path or a near-total strap/geometry loss; the SDD does not enumerate the failure condition itself.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a smaller subset of stations can produce complete restraint loss, the AND across all nine stations is too conservative and the tree should broaden to an OR over fewer-station combinations.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012-TL top-event OR gate and the all-stations AND sub-gate

citations.quote: There is no redundancy in the hold floor hard points.

assumptions.text: The hold-floor hard points / saddle attachment constitute a single non-redundant load path that is itself a potential single point of failure (order-1 cut set).
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states no redundancy in the hard points; whether this qualifies as structure (substantiated by structural analysis/PRA) rather than a functional basic event needs engineering disposition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If treated purely as structure substantiated outside the functional tree, this branch is removed from the FTA and handled via structural/particular-risk analysis instead.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012-TL top-event OR-gate first input (hard-point basic event)

citations.quote: Saddles are pinned to hard points in the hold floor beam structure.

assumptions.text: The restraint tension monitoring loop is indication only and does not itself provide or restore restraint, so it is not a contributor to loss of restraint.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states in-flight the crew has indication only with no in-flight adjustment of restraint; the loop is a monitor, not a restraint element.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loss of monitoring is deemed to defeat a credited crew mitigation, a monitor/detection branch (inhibit gate) would need adding.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of the tension-loop branch from SF-012-TL

citations.quote: In flight the crew has indication only; there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint.
